headline: US midterms shake Trump's grip on power, GTA 6 pre-orders hit $751M boosting TTWO, and the Roosters pip the Knights 19-18 in a thriller Grand Final.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Best mover in today's session, up 1.76%. Emerging markets got a lift as the US dollar softened slightly and risk appetite improved following the US midterm results, which markets saw as reducing the chance of sweeping new tariffs.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced 2.12% today — a welcome green day after a bruising run. No specific catalyst in today's news; likely a small technical rebound. The lithium price story remains difficult and the stock is still deeply underwater overall (-57% on your position), so this is a day's respite rather than a turning point.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Closed up 1.03% today, tracking last night's strong NASDAQ session (+1.09%). The US market got a boost from the midterm results reducing political uncertainty — this ETF gives you broad exposure to the whole US sharemarket.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Up 1.13% today on the ASX, riding the NASDAQ's strong night. Nvidia is in focus after a big analyst report flagged further upside — that's one of the ETF's core holdings. Still well down overall (-19%) but the AI infrastructure theme remains intact.

movers.name: DHHF Diversified ETF
movers.note: Nudged up 0.73% today. As a diversified all-world ETF it moves with global sentiment — the mild positive vibes from US midterms helped. Nothing dramatic, just steady.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Rose 0.71% last night. GTA 6 pre-order momentum is extraordinary — $751 million in pre-orders with two weeks still to go before release. Some analysts think the market is undervaluing the stock given this. Piracy risk was flagged (Take-Two cited a 10-20% film-industry piracy rate), but that's a known risk, not a new shock.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Gained 0.78% last night, a solid small move. The main news is Alphabet's $15 billion Malaysia data centre investment facing some investor scrutiny over AI capital expenditure levels. Still, the NASDAQ's strong night carried it up. Long-term story is intact.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Barely moved today, up just 0.16%. VDHG is a broadly diversified fund so it absorbs good and bad news across dozens of markets simultaneously — a quiet day is entirely normal. It's also been flagged by Morningstar as one of the ETFs growing in popularity with Australian investors, which is a nice long-term tailwind.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Dipped 0.99% last night — the only red mover in the portfolio. No specific bad news; this looks like profit-taking after a strong run. Microsoft is still up nearly 20% on your overall position, so one soft night changes nothing about the long-term story.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Good day but thesis still broken
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced 2.12% today, which is a nice green day — but the stock is still down 57% on your position and lithium prices remain depressed globally. There's no news today suggesting a structural recovery in lithium. For a long-term holder: sit tight and don't average down yet without a clear catalyst.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 momentum is real — hold with confidence
watch_today.detail: Pre-orders for GTA 6 have hit $751 million with two weeks still to go before release. That's a historic number for gaming. The stock ticked up 0.71% last night and the thesis is very much alive. No reason to sell ahead of what could be a massive launch catalyst.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF catching a bid — hold on
watch_today.detail: Up 1.13% today, tracking a strong NASDAQ night and positive Nvidia analyst coverage. The AI infrastructure theme is still the dominant technology story globally. Despite being down 19% overall, the long-run case for AI-exposed equities remains strong. Hold.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Small dip last night — nothing to worry about
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 0.99% last night with no specific negative catalyst. It's still up ~20% on your position. For a long-term holder this is just noise — the cloud and AI story remains one of the strongest in global tech. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike: watch your savings rates and mortgage costs
watch_today.detail: The RBA has hiked the cash rate again in November 2026, with savings platforms already advertising higher savings account rates. The RBA is also flagging that Australia's AI data centre building boom is itself inflationary — meaning rates could stay higher for longer. If you have a variable mortgage, factor this in. On the flip side, term deposits and savings accounts are paying more.

watch_today.title: US midterms: Republicans took a hit — tariff risk reduces
watch_today.detail: Democrats appear to have made significant gains in the US midterm elections, with Republicans taking 'big hits'. This matters for your portfolio because sweeping new tariffs (which Trump had been pushing) become harder to pass. That's a mild positive for emerging markets exposure (VGE.AX) and global trade generally.

world.summary: The US midterm elections dominate global news, with Republicans suffering significant losses and Trump vowing to lurch further right. Meanwhile, the Israel-Iran conflict continues to evolve, with Israel forming a new government and Trump playing down further strikes on Iran. A UK theme park was evacuated in a security incident and a Royal Navy submarine set a world record.

stories.title: Republicans take a hammering in US midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: The US midterm elections — the halfway-point vote that tests a president's popularity — have delivered a significant blow to Donald Trump's Republicans, with Democrats winning control of key races. Trump responded by saying the US took a 'giant step back' and signalled he intends to push even further right. Democrats are now planning their legislative agenda around healthcare and tariffs, but have ruled out pursuing impeachment. For Australian investors, a weakened Trump makes sweeping new tariffs less likely, which is a mild positive for global trade and emerging markets.

stories.title: Israel forms new government under Gadi Eisenkot
stories.why_it_matters: Israel's president has officially tasked former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government, marking a significant political shift in Israel. Eisenkot is a centrist military figure seen as more pragmatic than outgoing leadership. This comes amid ongoing conflict in the region following the 2026 Iran war, and signals potential changes in how Israel manages both the domestic political situation and its foreign policy stance.

stories.title: Trump plays down new strikes on Iran as conflict simmers
stories.why_it_matters: Despite the ongoing 2026 Iran conflict — which involves the US, Israel, and tensions over the Strait of Hormuz — Trump has signalled he wants to avoid further direct military strikes on Iran. Oil prices dipped slightly to $89.82/barrel, suggesting markets aren't pricing in an immediate escalation. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global oil supply, so any flare-up would spike energy prices fast. Worth monitoring.

stories.title: Royal Navy submarine breaks world record with 210-day patrol
stories.why_it_matters: A Royal Navy nuclear submarine has completed the longest continuous underwater patrol in history — 210 days at sea without surfacing. That breaks the previous record by a significant margin and underscores how modern nuclear subs operate in near-complete secrecy. It's a reminder of the strategic military capability underpinning Western deterrence, particularly relevant given current global tensions.

stories.title: Major security incident forces evacuation of UK theme park
stories.why_it_matters: A major UK theme park was closed and fully evacuated after a 'security incident' on the weekend. Details remain limited, but the event was significant enough to trigger a full emergency response. A separate 'major incident' was also declared outside the OVO Hydro venue in Glasgow, with fights breaking out and police called en masse. Both events point to ongoing public safety challenges at large venues in the UK.

markets.summary: Last night the NASDAQ surged 1.09% and the S&P 500 crept up 0.31%, both lifted by US midterm results reducing political uncertainty. The ASX 200 had a quiet session today, closing just 0.1% higher. Gold hit $4,107/oz — continuing its strong run. Oil slipped slightly to $89.82. The Aussie dollar weakened to 68.87 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Barely moved today — a flat, uneventful session on the local market.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's modest gain driven by post-midterm relief — markets like reduced political uncertainty.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's standout. Tech stocks jumped over 1% as the midterm results signalled less risk of sweeping tech regulation under a weakened Republican Congress.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Slipped just over 1% — Trump's comments playing down further Iran strikes eased fears of a supply disruption through the Strait of Hormuz.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold continues to march higher, hitting another record. Ongoing geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East, US politics) is keeping demand for the safe-haven metal strong.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped to under 69 US cents. The RBA's rate hike hasn't been enough to prop it up against a broadly firmer US dollar.

politics.summary: The RBA has hiked rates again and is warning that Australia's AI data centre building boom is pushing up inflation — meaning rates could stay higher for longer. Labor is facing a tightening political race, with the Coalition closing the gap in the polls. A battle over AI copyright laws is heating up, with Australian artists urging the PM to stand up to tech giants.

stories.title: RBA hikes rates again, warns AI data centres are stoking inflation
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia has lifted the cash rate again in November 2026, with savings platforms already hiking deposit rates in response. More concerning: the RBA is explicitly linking Australia's boom in AI data centre construction to higher inflation — these facilities use enormous amounts of power and require massive infrastructure spend, which pushes up costs economy-wide. RBA's Hunter also noted that AI has yet to actually deliver productivity gains or cause job losses, meaning the economy is bearing the cost of AI investment without the efficiency benefits yet. Bottom line: rates are likely to stay higher for longer than many hoped.

stories.title: Coalition closes gap on Labor in latest polling
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports that the Coalition is closing in on Labor in the polls, described as a 'blow for PM' Albanese. No specific polling numbers are available from the article, but the direction of travel matters for markets — a potential change in government would bring different policies on energy, housing, and taxation.

stories.title: Labor tipped to offer gas policy concessions after industry backlash
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is reportedly preparing to offer concessions on its gas policy after a significant industry and community backlash. The nature of the concessions isn't detailed in the available article, but the retreat signals political pressure on Labor's energy transition agenda. This is relevant to energy companies and anyone watching Australia's gas export industry.

stories.title: Australian artists tell PM: stand up to AI giants on copyright
stories.why_it_matters: A coalition of Australian artists — including some described as 'Albanese's favourite artists' — have written to the PM urging him to 'tell AI giants where to shove it' over proposed copyright law changes. The core issue: AI companies want to use creative works for training their models without payment or permission. Meanwhile, a separate AFR report reveals that musicians are being pressured by AI firms to recreate tracks specifically so companies can secure copyright over AI-generated versions. This is a live policy fight with real consequences for Australia's creative industry.

stories.title: PM shelves plan to sell Defence sites despite audit recommending it
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese has scrapped plans to sell off Defence Department land and facilities, despite an official audit recommending the sell-off. The decision has a twist — it involves a golf course, with a 'sudden shift in sell-off policy' raising eyebrows. The move is being read as politically motivated, as selling Defence land is unpopular with local communities. It's unlikely to have major market implications but adds to the picture of a government making cautious pre-election calls.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the dominant AI theme globally right now, with the US midterms bringing pro-regulation Democrats into power and raising the prospect of stricter rules for tech giants. In Australia, the RBA has flagged AI's inflationary impact, while artists are fighting AI companies over copyright. NEAR Protocol launched a new open AI model for its cloud platform.

stories.title: Pro-AI regulation candidates win big in US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The US midterm results are being read as a defeat for the big AI companies: candidates who favour stronger AI regulation — including guardrails on what AI models can do and how they're built — won key races. Democrats now control the legislative agenda in at least one chamber, and while the party is divided internally on AI policy (some want to encourage innovation, others want strict rules), the direction is toward more oversight. For companies like Google and Microsoft, this could mean more compliance costs and limits on how they deploy AI products.

stories.title: RBA: AI is pushing up inflation in Australia right now
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia has made an unusual observation: the current AI data centre building boom is itself a source of inflation. These facilities require enormous amounts of power, land, cooling infrastructure, and construction — all of which push up prices. The RBA's Sarah Hunter also noted that despite all the hype, AI has not yet delivered measurable productivity gains in the broader economy, meaning Australians are bearing the costs of the AI buildout without the promised efficiency benefits yet materialising.

stories.title: Australian artists fight back against AI copyright land grab
stories.why_it_matters: Australian musicians, writers, and visual artists have launched a public campaign urging PM Albanese to block proposed copyright law changes that would allow AI companies to scrape and use their creative work without permission or payment. Separately, the AFR reports that AI firms are pressuring musicians to re-record tracks specifically so the AI company can claim copyright over the resulting AI-generated versions — essentially using artists to do their legal groundwork for them. The government has not yet announced its position, and this is shaping up as a major creative industry battleground in 2026-27.

stories.title: NEAR Protocol launches new open-source AI model for its cloud platform
stories.why_it_matters: NEAR Protocol — a blockchain computing platform — has launched the Qwen 3.8 27B Abliterated AI model for its AI Cloud service. The model is open-source and aimed at developers building AI applications on its platform. It's a niche but notable move: it shows that AI model deployment is spreading beyond just the big tech players like Google and Microsoft, with decentralised platforms now offering competitive AI tools. Relevant background for GXAI.AX holders watching the broader AI ecosystem.

stories.title: Global push for AI regulation gathers pace
stories.source: The Asian Banker / Pearls and Irritations
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple commentators and financial industry bodies are calling for binding AI regulation — the debate is now less about 'if' and more about 'how'. Key questions include whether rules can be written clearly enough for businesses to follow, and whether regulators have the technical expertise to actually enforce them. For Australian investors in AI-exposed stocks (GXAI.AX, GOOG, MSFT), the direction of travel globally is toward more oversight, which creates compliance costs but also legitimises the technology by reducing the 'wild west' reputational risk.

sport.summary: In an extraordinary NRL Grand Final, the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in one of the tightest deciders in years. Off the field, the NRL has handed down a drink-driving ban to a Broncos star, an Eels recruit faces suspension over a World Cup referee gesture, and an Origin forward snubs Canberra for a big contract elsewhere.

stories.title: Roosters beat Knights 19-18 in a Grand Final classic
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters are the 2026 NRL premiers, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a heart-stopping Grand Final at Accor Stadium on Sunday evening. Just one point separated the two sides at the final whistle — the kind of finish that burns into rugby league folklore. The game went down to the wire in front of a packed stadium.

stories.title: Broncos star handed NRL drink-driving ban
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL has handed down a suspension to a Brisbane Broncos player following a drink-driving incident. The specific player's name and length of ban aren't confirmed in the available article text, but the NRL's announcement today marks a formal disciplinary outcome. The timing is notable — coming right after the Grand Final — and highlights the league's ongoing off-field conduct challenges.

stories.title: Star Eels recruit faces ban for World Cup referee gesture
stories.why_it_matters: A newly recruited Parramatta Eels player is facing an NRL ban following a controversial gesture directed at a referee during the recent Rugby League World Cup. The incident has been referred to the NRL judiciary. The player's specific identity and the nature of the gesture aren't confirmed in the available text, but the story is a significant off-season talking point as clubs prepare for 2027.

stories.title: Origin forward snubs Canberra, makes big contract call after PNG tour
stories.why_it_matters: A State of Origin forward — who toured Papua New Guinea with one of the rep sides — has publicly ruled out signing with the Canberra Raiders, saying 'nothing against Canberra' but opting to pursue a contract elsewhere. The player's identity isn't confirmed in the available text. It's a significant recruitment story heading into the 2027 season, with rival clubs set to benefit from Canberra missing out.
